intervals.label: collaboration (DM-Ice17 deployment to joint COSINE-100 run)
intervals.note: Lower bound: the DM-Ice17 deployment (December 2010); the collaboration's founding date is not published. End: the last DM-Ice paper read (2017).
intervals.quote: DM-Ice17, the first stage of the DM-Ice experimental program, was deployed at the geographic South Pole in December 2010 [36].

intervals.label: completed (programme joined COSINE-100)
intervals.note: No source read states that the DM-Ice Collaboration ended; this records that the programme's next step was the joint COSINE-100 run (2016 proceedings) and that the last DM-Ice paper read dates from 2017.
intervals.quote: We also discuss the plan and projected sensitivity of a new joint physics run, COSINE-100, with upgraded detectors at the Yangyang Underground Laboratory in Korea.

name: DM-Ice Collaboration
notes: No roster or member count was found; the Atlas records no memberships. The status is 'completed' with low confidence: it follows the end of DM-Ice17's physics run and the move of the programme into COSINE-100.
The collaboration's website (dm-ice.physics.wisc.edu, redirecting to dm-ice.yale.edu) could not be read beyond a redirect notice, so no website is recorded on the collaboration.

summary.plain: The collaboration that built DM-Ice17, a small sodium-iodide dark matter detector frozen into the Antarctic ice next to IceCube at the South Pole, and planned a larger detector there to test the yearly signal claimed by DAMA.
summary.technical: DM-Ice Collaboration, led from the Wisconsin IceCube Particle Astrophysics Center (University of Wisconsin-Madison) with other institutions (the project page later moved to Yale). After DM-Ice17 the programme joined the COSINE-100 effort ('a new joint physics run, COSINE-100', arXiv:1612.07426).
